items.title: TeraWulf adds conditional Google backstop and Fluor construction contract at Justified
items.summary: TeraWulf’s November 4 filing describes Google credit support for certain Anthropic obligations under existing Justified leases in Kentucky. The backstop becomes effective for each lease when its final data hall starts. Following specified tenant defaults, Google can assume the lease and pay rent or, in certain circumstances, pay a termination fee that entitles it to an equity interest in the project subsidiary. The approximately $19 billion is existing lease commitments, not a new loan or another lease to add. A separate Fluor engineering, procurement and construction agreement covers three buildings; guaranteed maximum pricing is still being established. Phased service is expected from late 2027 through Q2 2028. These are financing and execution milestones, while debt funding and delivered capacity remain prospective.

TeraWulf announces Google credit support and definitive Fluor EPC agreement

items.impact_reason: Conditional credit support and a definitive construction agreement advance a substantial regional AI campus. Effectiveness conditions, debt funding and future delivery limit immediate supply implications.
items.confidence: High for the filed contractual terms; financing benefits and service milestones remain forward-looking.
items.event_date_scope: Agreements and announcement; the underlying Anthropic lease was announced July 6. Editorial review is November 5.
items.future_target: Phased ready-for-service completions expected from late 2027 through Q2 2028; no operating capacity established here.

items.title: Coherent’s datacenter and communications sales rise 79% to $1.95B
items.summary: Coherent’s November 4 results show $1.9517 billion of Datacenter & Communications revenue for the quarter ended September 30, compared with $1.0900 billion a year earlier. That is 79.1% growth calculated from its segment table. Company-wide revenue was $2.3703 billion, up about 50%. The expansion is a substantial commercial signal from an optical-component supplier serving AI infrastructure, but the segment also includes communications products and is not AI-only revenue. Sales dollars do not establish how much networking capacity is installed, utilized or available to AI users. The report supports strong supplier demand without resolving downstream construction and power constraints.

items.title: AMD’s data-center revenue nearly doubles to $8.55B as MI450 systems reach customers
items.summary: AMD’s November 3 earnings release reports $8.546 billion of Data Center revenue for the quarter ended September 26, up 97% year over year. AMD attributes growth to EPYC processors and the launch of Instinct MI450 GPUs, and says Anthropic, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI and Oracle are running workloads on the first Helios systems. This is evidence of commercial momentum for another large AI infrastructure supplier, but the segment includes CPUs and other products: it is not GPU-only sales or an installed-accelerator count. AMD’s approximately $17 billion fourth-quarter outlook is company-wide guidance, rather than a reported data-center result or a guarantee of future deliveries.

items.title: LandGate counts 819 US data-center announcements through October, above all of 2025
items.summary: LandGate’s November 4 report says 819 US data-center projects were announced in 2026 through October, exceeding its 764 for all of 2025. In its 6,561-project tracker, 3,045 are in development and 3,191 operating; 71% of the development pipeline is classified as hyperscale. The survey points to a large proposed buildout, while project counts do not measure megawatts, AI utilization or completed construction. LandGate identifies grid interconnection and local approvals as execution constraints. Its claim that capital has ceased to be the limiting factor is the research provider’s interpretation, not proof that every developer is funded. The tracked development pipeline must remain separate from operating supply.

items.title: DigitalOcean reports roughly 10× quarterly inference-token growth and $376M AI customer ARR
items.summary: DigitalOcean’s November 3 results report $321 million of revenue for the quarter ended September 30, up 40% year over year, and $376 million of AI Customer ARR, up 288%. That ARR annualizes the quarter’s revenue from customers using AI/ML offerings and includes their other cloud services; it is not inference-only revenue. Management says Inference Engine token volume grew roughly tenfold from the prior quarter, without disclosing an absolute count. It also says 20 incremental megawatts have been secured for 2028. The results support accelerating demand at this provider, while the token ratio supplies no platform-wide daily total and the future megawatts are not operating capacity.

items.title: OpenAI launches grid-flexibility program, building on Georgia’s up-to-1GW agreement
items.summary: OpenAI announced Grid Protectors on November 2 to negotiate demand-reduction arrangements for future compute campuses. Its pilot is the planned Effingham County, Georgia campus, whose agreement includes up to 1,000MW of flexible demand response once operating. Georgia Power disclosed that commitment on July 22 under a 25-year agreement for a facility expected to need approximately 3,200MW. The new announcement extends that model into a national program; it does not announce a new 1GW block of generation or an operating campus. Local response amounts, speed and duration will vary, and further commitments remain to be finalized. Grid flexibility could affect how large AI loads secure utility service, but delivered curtailment has not been established.

items.title: Marvell proposes $115B Lumentum acquisition to combine chip and optical connectivity
items.summary: Marvell and Lumentum announced on November 2 that Marvell would acquire Lumentum in an all-stock transaction with an implied enterprise value of $115 billion. Each Lumentum share would receive 4.500 Marvell shares. Combining Marvell’s interconnect and custom-silicon portfolio with Lumentum’s lasers, optical transceivers and optical switching could change how AI systems source connections between chips and data centers. That integration remains prospective: the companies expect closing in the first half of 2028, subject to both companies’ shareholder approvals, regulatory approvals and other conditions. The announced valuation is not cash investment in new compute capacity or evidence of measured performance gains.

items.title: Oracle prices $10B stock sale and $10B notes; closing expected November 4
items.summary: Oracle’s November 2 pricing release sets 86,206,897 common shares at $116 each, approximately $10 billion gross, alongside $10 billion of senior notes. The five debt tranches carry coupons from 7.000% to 8.650% and mature between 2029 and 2046. Both offerings are expected to close November 4, subject to customary conditions, and neither closing depends on the other. Pricing replaces the preliminary terms reported here earlier. The financing is material to a major cloud supplier, but proceeds have broad corporate uses; this does not establish completed fundraising, an AI-specific construction budget or delivered capacity.

items.title: Anthropic’s compute commitments carry different risks
items.summary: Anthropic’s November 2 amended S-1 describes minimum spending of $110 billion with AWS from May 2026 through April 2036 and $44.9 billion with Microsoft from November 2026 through June 2033, subject to specified exceptions. The Microsoft end date updates the earlier filing’s May 2033 date. SpaceX arrangements total up to $120.5 billion through 2029, but either party can cancel on 90 days’ notice after initial noncancelable periods ending in January and March 2027. Across purchase commitments and leases entered into as of and after September 30, Anthropic reports approximately $895.4 billion, largely for compute and infrastructure; $213.8 billion involves exercisable termination rights or conditions before commencement. These overlapping totals are not new deals to add together, supplier-recognized revenue or delivered capacity.

items.title: LG CNS reports completion of a 30MW-class AI data center in Jakarta
items.summary: LG CNS said on November 2 that it had completed a 30MW-class AI data center in Jakarta for KMG, a venture backed by Sinar Mas and Korea Investment Real Asset Management. The company says customers for its full capacity were secured before completion. This is a concrete regional construction milestone, while GPU deployment and utilization remain undisclosed. The first phase uses air cooling; liquid cooling is planned for later phases. A future expansion to 400MW of total incoming electrical capacity remains in design and must not be counted as completed capacity. The release does not establish a comparable IT-load figure or installed GPU count.
